spatial_claims.claim: Line t is tangent to the circle at T; line n passes through T perpendicular to t; O is the centre of the circle
OT is perpendicular to t (by 3.18, since t is tangent at T and O is the centre)
B is on n on the opposite side of t from O
A is on t distinct from T; ray TA lies along t
Angle OTA is a right angle (OT perpendicular to t)
Angle ATB is a right angle (n perpendicular to t, B on n)
TO and TB lie on opposite sides of line TA
Adjacent angles OTA + ATB = two right angles
By 1.14, TO and TB lie in one straight line (collinear)
Since TB lies on n and T,O,B are collinear, O lies on n

configuration_map: T is the point of tangency on the circle and on line t. Line n passes through T perpendicular to t, extending to both sides of t. O is the centre of the circle, not on t (since OT perp t with O distinct from T by positive radius). O lies on one side of t. A is a point on t distinct from T, so ray TA lies along t. B is a point on n on the opposite side of t from O, distinct from T. Rays TO and TB emanate from T to opposite sides of line t. Both angles OTA and ATB are right angles (90 degrees each), summing to 180 degrees (two right angles). By 1.14, T-O-B are collinear. Since T and B both lie on n and are distinct, the line through them is n, so O lies on n.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof uses a direct approach via 1.14 (collinearity from adjacent angles summing to two right angles) rather than Heath's proof by contradiction. The key spatial facts — O and B on opposite sides of t, both angles being right angles, 1.14 applicability — are all compatible. No angle decomposition errors, no interior/exterior contradictions, and no conflicting implicit assumptions.
